section_summary: This section opens with a request for evidence about espionage by Japanese businesses in the United States, then follows the recruitment, work, and reception of a State–War Department mission studying the zaibatsu. It also contains reports of Soviet criticism of American occupation policy and a State Department account of proposed limits on Japanese industry. The final pages begin a collection of prewar agreements between Japanese and foreign firms, including patent and technology licenses.

subfiles.title: Subversive Activities of Japanese Businesses in the U.S.
subfiles.about: Requests a consolidated FBI study of espionage by Japanese business concerns in the United States.
subfiles.summary: The Commodities Division seeks evidence for its study of Japanese cartels and business–government ties.

subfiles.title: State–War Mission to Study Standards for Disestablishment of Japanese Combines
subfiles.about: Reports mission recruitment and seeks salary clearance for experts from several agencies.
subfiles.summary: The War Department will cover mission expenses except government employees’ salaries. Rudolph lists prospective members and asks Thorp to obtain agency approvals.

subfiles.title: Justice Department nominations for the zaibatsu mission
subfiles.about: Nominates Antitrust Division lawyers and requests clarification of the mission’s authority and support.
subfiles.summary: Berge proposes William Butz, William Dixon, and Posey Kime, describes efforts to recruit other specialists, and distinguishes policy work from the War Department’s implementation role. He asks for clear authority, staff, background material, and living arrangements.

subfiles.title: Justice Department salary approval for mission personnel
subfiles.about: Agrees to keep four Justice Department personnel on salary during the mission.
subfiles.summary: Justice will pay salaries if another agency covers travel and living expenses.

subfiles.title: Federal Trade Commission detail of Robert B. Dawkins
subfiles.about: Authorizes Dawkins’s mission assignment and FTC salary payments.
subfiles.summary: The FTC details Dawkins despite a pending Comptroller General decision, noted as received later that day.

subfiles.title: Tariff Commission detail of Benjamin B. Wallace
subfiles.about: Approves Wallace’s mission service with salary paid by the Tariff Commission.
subfiles.summary: The War Department will cover Wallace’s other expenses.

subfiles.title: Securities and Exchange Commission detail of Raymond Vernon
subfiles.about: Authorizes Vernon’s service on the zaibatsu mission.
subfiles.summary: The SEC will pay Vernon’s salary; the War Department will cover other expenses.

subfiles.title: Additional Justice Department nominations
subfiles.about: Nominates Robert Hunter and Benjamin Wallace for the zaibatsu mission.
subfiles.summary: Avery provides their qualifications, reports Frank Graham’s unavailability, and notes continuing recruitment efforts.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketch of James McI. Henderson
subfiles.about: Provides Henderson’s background for mission selection.
subfiles.summary: Avery highlights Henderson’s antitrust experience, judgment, and leadership of West Coast offices.

subfiles.title: Possible addition of Frank Tamagna to the mission
subfiles.about: Urges quick consideration of Tamagna for the zaibatsu mission.
subfiles.summary: Tamagna needs an immediate answer before accepting another War Department opportunity.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the head of the zaibatsu mission
subfiles.about: Sets the mission’s reporting arrangements and logistical support in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The joint State–War mission is to recommend policy for disestablishing the combines and report to both secretaries. In Japan it will operate under the Supreme Commander, who is asked to provide access, facilities, and assistance.

subfiles.title: Request to transmit an urgent message to Edwards
subfiles.about: Asks the War Department to cable an enclosed message to Edwards in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Terrill notes Edwards’s work with Colonel Wheeler of SCAP’s Economic and Scientific Section.

subfiles.title: Recommendations of Mission on Japanese Combines
subfiles.about: Summarizes ten recommendations for breaking up zaibatsu power.
subfiles.summary: Proposals cover dissolution, family divestment, stock sales, antitrust law, taxes, cooperatives, and public education.

subfiles.title: Appreciation for Raymond Vernon’s mission service
subfiles.about: Thanks the SEC for Vernon’s work on the mission.
subfiles.summary: Thorp praises Vernon and cites General Marquat’s commendation of the mission.

subfiles.title: Appreciation for Robert Dawkins’s mission service
subfiles.about: Thanks the FTC for Dawkins’s work on the mission.
subfiles.summary: Thorp praises Dawkins and cites General Marquat’s commendation.

subfiles.title: Fragment of correspondence on economic concentration
subfiles.about: Only a few OCR words concerning concentration are legible.
subfiles.summary: The document cannot be identified reliably from the surviving OCR.

subfiles.title: Proposal to thank agencies for zaibatsu mission assistance
subfiles.about: Suggests sending appreciation letters after the mission’s return.
subfiles.summary: Rudolph notes that Edwards’s report is being duplicated.

subfiles.title: Appreciation for Justice Department mission members
subfiles.about: Thanks Justice for Henderson, Dixon, and Neel’s mission service.
subfiles.summary: Thorp praises their work and cites General Marquat’s commendation.

subfiles.title: Postponement of Edwards’s Washington visit
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, conveying Henry Owen’s message
subfiles.about: Moves Edwards’s Washington visit from September 3 to September 9.
subfiles.summary: The telegram cites Sherwood Fine’s vacation and mentions a hotel reservation.

subfiles.title: Pravda editorial on zaibatsu and American policy
subfiles.about: Summarizes M. Markov’s criticism of occupation policy in Pravda.
subfiles.summary: The editorial accuses Japanese combines of wartime collaboration and argues that American business ties and occupation policy are preserving zaibatsu influence.

subfiles.title: U.S. Program for Reaching Level of Industry Decisions for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the status of U.S. proposals on Japanese industrial capacity.
subfiles.summary: Martin outlines interim reparations cuts, assured retention levels, general policy papers, and planned industry limits. He explains delays involving Far Eastern Commission debate, SCAP comments, and trade forecasts, and links reparations removals to security based limits.

subfiles.title: Izvestiya article on Japan and American monopolies
subfiles.about: Summarizes V. Yarovoi’s Izvestiya article alleging American support for Japanese monopolies.
subfiles.summary: The article asserts that American firms seek markets and investments in Japan while Japanese concerns seek to preserve their position. It portrays zaibatsu dissolution as slow and largely superficial, citing the limited securities surrendered by major combines.

subfiles.title: Correction concerning deconcentration proposals
subfiles.about: Clarifies that the Far Eastern Commission has not considered the U.S. deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: Rudolph proposes replacement wording for Borton’s letter to Professor Colegrove.

subfiles.title: Zaibatsu Mission Report sent to Professor Colegrove
subfiles.about: Sends the mission report and explains the omission of classified recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Borton says funding and personnel are major obstacles to faster dissolution.

subfiles.title: Transmission of zaibatsu foreign contracts
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of contracts between zaibatsu and foreign firms.
subfiles.summary: The contracts were supplied through Judge Spencer’s office at SCAP.

subfiles.title: International Contracts
subfiles.about: Lists contracts between Japanese firms and foreign companies.
subfiles.summary: The index identifies roughly eighty contracts involving Japanese manufacturers and firms in the United States, Europe, and Canada. It precedes copies of selected agreements.

subfiles.title: Verreries de la Gare patent assignment offer to Asahi Glass
subfiles.from: Verreries de la Gare et A. Belotte Réunies
subfiles.about: Offers Asahi Glass exclusive rights to a glass furnace invention in Japan, China, and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The French firm sets out patent, technical drawing, improvement sharing, training, and payment terms. The proposed price is 100,000 francs.

subfiles.title: Morita’s acceptance with amendment to technician visits
subfiles.to: Verreries de la Gare et A. Belotte Réunies
subfiles.about: Accepts the patent agreement while requesting training for two or three technicians.
subfiles.summary: Morita reproduces the proposed terms and asks the French firm to amend the training clause, which allows only one technician.

subfiles.title: Approval of two Asahi Glass trainees
subfiles.from: Verreries de la Gare et A. Belotte Réunies
subfiles.about: Agrees that two technicians may train at its works.
subfiles.summary: The firm also promises to send the required plans.

subfiles.title: Fuji Electric report on its Siemens contracts and registered rights
subfiles.about: Discloses Fuji Electric’s Siemens contracts, royalties, and registered patents, utility models, and designs.
subfiles.summary: The disclosure describes a long running technology arrangement with Siemens covering electrical equipment and communications apparatus. It lists royalties already paid and outstanding, explains how payments were handled, and attaches extensive registration schedules.

subfiles.title: Aluminium Laboratories–Furukawa patent license
subfiles.about: Licenses patents for transmission cable fittings and related technology in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The agreement grants Furukawa a license with restricted sublicensing rights and sets royalties on sales. An attached schedule identifies Japanese and Manchukuo patents and a utility model.

subfiles.title: Long Distance Cable Agreement between Furukawa and Siemens
subfiles.from: Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd. and Siemens & Halske
subfiles.to: Furukawa Electric Co., Ltd. and Siemens & Halske
subfiles.about: Renews arrangements for territorial patent licenses and technology exchange concerning long distance cables.
subfiles.summary: The agreement defines covered cable products and assigns Furukawa territories in Japan and Manchukuo and Siemens territories in much of Europe, with shared rights in China. It provides reciprocal licenses, limits sales outside assigned territories, addresses patents and confidential experience, and specifies annual compensation and royalties. The agreement continues beyond page 79.
